FILED s543m (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-24), found by member 2's probes (#5374).  PRE-EXISTING: base 9fc6583b the same.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 | ./runpcl; scratch/s543m/p2/f.pl line f9):
    { package Q9; our $w9 = 1; my $w9 = 4; print "f9 ", $w9 + 1, " $Q9::w9\n"; }
  perl  f9 5 1        PCL  f9 5 4

WHAT IT IS (suspect, not measured): a FILE-LEVEL bare block that opens with `package Q9;` is flattened into its own section (read in-package Q9), so the lexical `my $w9` is a `let` of the symbol `$w9` interned in Q9 -- and the qualified spelling `$Q9::w9` IS that symbol: the `let` shadows the package variable for every spelling of it (the my-shadow mechanism).  #470's rule (a file that spells the package variable qualified takes the mangle for the lexical) covers a PROMOTED file lexical; this one is an ordinary `let` in the section.  Also check `package Q9; my $v = 4; print $Q9::v` at the top level (no block) and `$main::x` beside a top-level `my $x` in main.
subject: SILENT WRONG: in a file-level `{ package Q9; our $w9 = 1; my $w9 = 4; ... }` the qualified `$Q9::w9` reads the LEXICAL (perl 1, PCL 4)
